items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: So there was Gus Aikin, Red Allen and some other trumpet player... And we started to play... So I made the mistake of, you know, like coming in on his chorus, and I screamed like a G.

ctx.x: you." And all I said, when you asked me...

See, what happens... Let me explain something to you, what happened. When I left here, the trumpet players that were of any note had their own individual sound. You could tell Louis if you heard him, you could tell Cootie if you heard him -- right? You could tell Bobby Starks if you heard him. You could tell Red Allen if you heard him. You could tell Lips Page. Any of those cats that were like the big cats of the day, they had their own distinct sound. And they all had some kind of vibrato, you know.
